question: Can I walk to the petroglyphs at Kejimkujik on my own as a member of the general public?
generated_answer:
Yes, you can walk to the petroglyphs at Kejimkujik on your own. However, it's important to note that the petroglyphs are located in a remote area of the park and the trails can be challenging. It's recommended to bring plenty of water, wear appropriate hiking gear, and consider bringing a map or GPS device. Additionally, be respectful of the site and keep a safe distance from the petroglyphs to help preserve them for future generations. 

If you're not comfortable hiking on your own or want more information about the site, guided tours are also available. These tours are led by knowledgeable park staff or local guides who can provide more context and insights about the petroglyphs and the Mi'kmaq culture. 

Remember to check with park staff for any specific regulations or guidelines before heading out, as conditions and accessibility can vary depending on the time of year and weather. 

Here is a map of the park to help you plan your visit: [Kejimkujik National Park and National Historic Site Map](https://www.pc.gc.ca/en/pn-np/ns/kejimkujik/visit/plan)

Enjoy your visit to Kejimkujik!
